Original learning chapter · updated 9 September 2026. Equations and examples explain concepts; they are not test acceptance or a support matrix.

Prerequisites: 01 · Vectors, lengths and coordinate systems, 03 · Triangles, area and surface normals, 11 · Derivatives, backpropagation and fitting

A scene organizes; a renderer evaluates

A mesh describes geometry. A scene says which material belongs to it, which camera observes it and how it is positioned relative to other objects. The minimal gffx scene is one in-memory container, not a file format or editor. A rig is a transform group here, not a skinning solver. Camera and light payloads retain explicit world matrices for the integrator; flatten does not secretly evaluate them.

Local coordinates become world coordinates

With column-vector matrices, multiply parent world transform by child local transform. Order matters: translating a scaled object is different from scaling its translation. A parent translating two units, a child translating three and a mesh translating four produce a nine-unit translation. Parenting is continuous matrix arithmetic, so gradients can flow back to each transform.

Normal directions are not ordinary points

Normals have no translation. Under nonuniform scale, applying the same linear map as a point generally breaks perpendicularity. Use the inverse transpose and renormalize. The signed determinant accounts for winding reversal under reflection in this contract. For A = diag(-2,1,1), a normal proportional to (1,1,1) becomes proportional to (0.5,-1,-1).

Four places an attribute can live

Constant means one value per object; uniform means one per face; vertex means one per vertex; face-varying means one per face corner. Two faces can share a position vertex yet use different UVs across a seam. Packing to corner values preserves that distinction. A missing attribute gets an explicit presence mask, not an invented default material value.

Worked example: flattening is bookkeeping, not geometry repair

Suppose two triangle meshes have three vertices each. The second mesh's local face (0,1,2) becomes (3,4,5). Frame boundaries are [0,6] for vertices and [0,2] for faces. Two frames use vertex boundaries [0,6,12] and face boundaries [0,2,4]. All objects in a frame render together; they do not accidentally become separate image batches. Shared input topology is repeated and rebased in the packed output, so shared topology does not mean zero output memory.

Try it yourself

A second frame repeats the two triangles above. What are its globally indexed faces?

Answer

(6,7,8) and (9,10,11). The frame starts at vertex 6 and contains both objects.

gffx boundary: what the derivative test establishes

The scene tests perturb a small translation away from visibility changes, rasterize and interpolate colours, and compare reverse-mode gradients with finite differences. A fresh step must reduce image error. This proves a smooth local path through flatten, not gradients through changing topology or hard visibility boundaries. Compilation/export and a full gffit optimizer are separate acceptance questions.
